_what: one block per model, and a block that is not there is a model that runs on whatever the client asked for. A key that is missing from a block takes the value the client sent, so a block with only a system is a block that changes the rules and nothing else.
_how_it_applies: the proxy adds these to the request before it reaches Ollama: system goes as a system message, and the rest go into options. The log shows what the client sent and what was added, so a wrong answer can be traced to a setting here rather than to the model.
_rules_live_in_files: system names a file under VSCode/rules/, not the text itself. A rule that lives in this file cannot be read, diffed, or given a history, and the whole point of editing rules per model is that the file is the thing a person opens.
_note_on_num_predict: not set here on purpose. A cap that is too small truncates the answer in the middle of a sentence, and a truncated answer looks like a model that stopped thinking. Set it per request when a run must be short.
